findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no hot water to be available at hand sink. Discussed with PIC, hot water will be serviced. Ensure hot water is available at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed walk in cooler to have an ambient temperature of 45F-47F. Discussed with PIC, walk in cooler was observed to be set at 50F. Setting was dropped down to 40F. Inspector will follow up  Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F. 

Later during inspection, walk in cooler was observed to have dropped to 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed walk in cooler to have an ambient temperature of 45F-47F. Discussed with PIC, walk in cooler will be serviced. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple sandwiches to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, sandwiches were pulled and discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed door to walk in cooler to be in a state of disrepair. Multiple holes were observed and pieces of the door are missing. Discussed with PIC, walk in cooler issues are believed to be separate from door issues, however PIC will look into replacing door. Ensure equipment is working up to the manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is made and at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bottle was set up and teste at 200 ppm(Quat). Ensure sanitizer solution is set up at all hours of operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed coving to be missing around the perimeter of the employee bathroom in places. Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before the next routine inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

(REPEAT) Observed no Norovirus clean-up policy. Policy was provided during the last routine inspection due to lack of procedural documentation. Provided new copy of the policy. Facility has bleach to perform the procedure. Post on a wall near the mop sink in the back or in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/31/22.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed the hand sink in the kitchen to have a gap between the wall and sink. Caulking has come away. Re-caulk the sink to the wall. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection on 3/31/22.

Other areas of the facility in need of repairs include:
1. Coving is missing around the perimeter of the employee bathroom in places
2. Hand sink in the main gas station area (near the coffee and hot holding area) has caulking coming away from the sink and wall - re-caulk the hand sink.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

No reporting agreements available during the inspection. PIC stated that the previous ones were likely discarded at the end of the past year. Inspector stated that these items should be maintained at all times at the facility and not discarded. PIC stated that they were the primary employee to handle foods at the facility. They filled out a SCDPH Reporting Agreement and took multiple copies for the other employees.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

No vomit/ diarrhea clean up procedure available during this inspection. A procedure acquired from the CDC was provided during the inspection to correct. PIC is aware that they must maintain a written procedure at all times at the facility.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

The single service spoons and forks dispensed by employees to consumers are observed in styrofoam cups that have soiled bottoms (inside where the food contact surfaces of the single service utensils make contact). Discussed with the PIC and the cups (with utensils) were discarded during the inspection. PIC was told that the containers should be maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The hand sink in the food prep area is observed with a gap between the sink and the wall. It appears that the caulking has cracked. PIC is instructed to re-caulk so that the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machines are observed with an accumulation of slime. PIC was consulted and the nozzles were washed/rinsed/sanitized during the inspection. PIC stated that employees are supposed to soak the nozzles every night and he washed them every couple days.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

No reporting agreements are observable at the facility at the time of the inspection. Extra copies were given to the PIC and he is instructed to ensure that employees sign and that a copy of each is maintained at the facility for inspector's observation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Raw chicken is observed at 46 degrees internal temperature in the walk in cooler. The chicken was discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: 1) 6-202.13  (C) A bug zapper is observed over the steam table in the front area. The bug zapper was moved during the inspection so as not to potentially contaminate foods. 2) 6-501.111  (Pf) Multiple flies are observed in the back area of the facility. PIC is instructed to ensure that pests are brought to a manageable level.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single use forks and spoons are observed stored with the eating ends standing up in the cups used for storage. The eating ends are also mixed in with the handles of other forks/spoons in the cups. The items were shifted so that the eating ends are all pointing down in the cups and protected form hand contamination.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

Milk was observed in the stand up cooler in the back of the facility at 45-50 degrees. Discussed with the person in charge (PIC) and the milk was moved to be taken home during the inspection.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

1) Observed the ice chute of the left soda fountain machine to have pink slime accumulating on the inner surfaces. 2) Observed the inner surfaces of the individual soda nozzles of the right soda fountain machine to be soiled with a dark slime. Discussed the violations with the PIC and instructed to clean (including taking apart the nozzles) often enough to prevent the accumulation of filth.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

Observed the deflector shield in the ice machine to have points at both the right and left corners with a thick layer of slime built up. Inspector discussed the cleaning practices with the PIC and instructed to clean and sanitize often enough so as to prevent the contamination of ready to eat foods (ice) by either pathogens or cleaning chemicals.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
The bucket of sanitizer in the  cooking area was observed to be at approximately 25-50 parts per million (ppm) Quat. Quat sanitizers have a minimum of 150 ppm concentration for effective sanitizing. The bucket was changed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

Multiple flies were observed in the cooking area and the area around the steam table. Discussed option for minimizing the amount of pests with the PIC (including suitable locations for fly strips and the use of air curtains) and will follow up in 3 weeks to check the progress.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. 
Observed chilli in the walk in cooler to be marked 12/18. Chilli should have been discarded 12/24. Chilli was discarded during the inspection.

750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service. 
Observed cooler with milk in the back of the facility to be at ~52 degrees. The delivery was received at 10 this morning. Milk was moved to a cooler capable of maintaining temperature during the inspection.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

Observed single service spoons and forks to be stored with the handles and the eating ends together. All utensils were moved (with gloves on) so the handles all lined up with each other and the potential for contamination was removed.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed corn dogs stored in a grocery sack. Food must be stored in food grade containers.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed an employee drink in the food prep area. Employee drinks must be stored in a designated area away from food. Drinks should have a lid and straw.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the upright freezer to have some frost accumulation. Defrost the freezer. 2) Observed duct tape on the sandwich cooler.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) coffee spout. 2) Ice chute on the Coca-Cola and Pepsi machines. 3) Ice machine deflector shield. Clean the food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the microwave to be soiled with food splash in the top and bottom of the microwave. Wash, rinse and sanitize the inside of the microwave.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service gloves stored on the floor in the kitchen area. Single service gloves must be stored at least 6" off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed an absence of paper towels at the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Replace the paper towels.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed an absence of coving near the soda machine. Replace coving.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed missing caulk behind the mop sink in the back room. Recaulk the mop sink to the wall in the back room.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed one manager that is awaiting the state certificate. Will follow up in 90 days to determine if the state certifcate has been received.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: No FSSMC

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice chute to have some mold accumulation. Clean the food contact surfaces as needed.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No full time FSSMC on site for inspection. The owner has taken the class but needs to take the exam to be recertified.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.citation_text: 750.1230 Observed no light shields on bulbs in cooler holding milk and landshire sandwiches. Provide shields.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750.880b Observed coffee filters stored uncovered.  The filters were moved during the inspection.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g Observed no chlorine test kit for facility.  Provide a test kit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 Observed raw wood underneath the soda machines.  Paint or seal the raw wood.
